questions.question: Which of the following is true about the melting point of rock?
options: It is very low.
It is very high.
It is exactly the same as water.
Rocks cannot melt under any conditions.

questions.question: What is melted rock called when it is underground?
options: Lava
Magma
Granite
Basalt

questions.question: Where does extrusive igneous rock form?
options: Deep inside Earth's mantle
Inside Earth's crust
Outside Earth's crust
In Earth's core

questions.question: What main factor determines the size of crystals in cooled igneous rock?
options: The rate at which the melted rock cools
The amount of water present in the rock
The type of fossils embedded in the rock
The atmospheric pressure above the rock

questions.question: Which of the following describes the types of grains that rocks can contain?
options: Only perfectly square grains
Round or interlocking grains
Only liquid-filled grains
Grains that are always invisible

questions.question: How are atoms arranged inside a crystal?
options: In a random, chaotic jumble
In a very regular pattern
In loose, moving layers
In hollow, air-filled spheres

questions.question: What conditions between tectonic plates allow large crystals to grow inside solid rock?
options: Extremely low temperatures and zero pressure
High pressure and high temperature
The presence of rushing surface water
Rapid freezing at the surface

questions.question: Under what conditions do metamorphic rocks form, altering their original structures?
options: Rapid cooling at the Earth's surface
Extreme pressure and temperature
Slow evaporation of salty lakes
Gentle accumulation of sand and mud

questions.question: Why do some metamorphic rocks easily separate into thin, flat sheets?
options: Because they contain round, loose sand grains
Because their crystals are aligned
Because they are made entirely of liquid magma
Because they cooled very rapidly on the surface

questions.question: What do rocks consist of?
options: Only pure liquid elements
Minerals and rock fragments
Fossilised wood only
Man-made synthetic chemicals

questions.question: What is a mineral?
options: A man-made mixture of different plastics
A naturally occurring pure substance with a crystal structure
Any rock that contains animal fossils
A type of organic soil used for farming

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the shape and outer structure of the Earth?
options: A flat disc with a thick crust, entirely covered in ice
A spherical, rocky planet with a thin crust, partially covered in water
A perfect cube made of solid iron, with no water
A gaseous sphere with a thick crust, completely dry

questions.question: What is the dense, rocky layer located directly under Earth's crust called?
options: The outer core
The inner core
The mantle
The atmosphere

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the centre of the Earth?
options: A liquid core surrounded by solid mantle
A solid metallic core surrounded by a liquid outer core
A hollow space filled with pressurized gas
A core made entirely of liquid water

questions.question: How do temperature and pressure change towards the centre of Earth, and what is the state of the inner core?
options: They decrease, making the inner core liquid
They increase, making the inner core extremely hot and solid
They stay constant, keeping the inner core gas
They increase, making the inner core a cold liquid

questions.question: What evidence supports the idea that Earth's continents were once all joined together?
options: The fact that all oceans are exactly the same depth
Rock formations and fossils
The identical weather patterns on all continents today
The presence of active volcanoes on every island

questions.question: What are the slowly moving pieces that Earth's crust is broken into called?
options: Glaciers
Tectonic plates
Mantle plumes
Sandy grains

questions.question: Which features are characteristic of sedimentary rocks?
options: Large interlocking crystals aligned in one direction
Distinct grains that are stuck together
Glassy textures with no distinct grains
Liquid layers that flow easily

questions.question: How do the crystals in igneous rocks compare to those in metamorphic rocks?
options: Igneous crystals point in many directions, while metamorphic crystals mostly line up
Igneous crystals are aligned, while metamorphic crystals point in many directions
Both rock types contain crystals that are perfectly round and do not point anywhere
Neither rock type contains any crystals at all

questions.question: What makes a rock non-porous rather than porous?
options: Containing round grains that do not touch
Containing interlocking grains or interlocking crystals
Being made completely of organic fossil shells
Having large air gaps between its fragments
